we run 5+ Claude Code agents in parallel on the same codebase using git worktrees and it works surprisingly well. each agent gets its own worktree so they can't step on each other's files. the orchestration is just tmux sessions with a coordinator that assigns tasks and merges results back. the tricky part is shared state - if two agents need to modify the same file you need a merge step. we solved it by having the coordinator detect conflicts and re-assign one of the tasks. isolation via worktrees is way simpler than containers for this use case since you keep full git history access.

here's our tmux-based agent orchestration setup if you want to see how the worktree isolation works in practice: https://github.com/m13v/tmux-background-agents/blob/main/SKILL.md - and the browser lock system for when multiple agents need to share a browser session: https://github.com/m13v/browser-lock/blob/main/playwright-lock.sh

I checked `origin/dev` again before writing this comment. As of today, this issue still appears unresolved in the tree:

- `packages/app/src/context/file/path.ts` still preserves native Windows separators in `normalize()`
- `packages/app/src/context/file/watcher.ts` still bails out on `add` / `unlink` when the immediate parent is not loaded instead of walking up to the nearest loaded ancestor
- the issue is still open

I attempted an upstream fix in PR #17794 and ended up closing it after multiple rounds because I could not get it to a trustworthy state within a reasonable cost budget.

What I changed in that attempt

1. Watcher / open-file path normalization on Windows
   - normalized watcher-side paths so `\` and `/` stop diverging between watcher events and store/tab keys
   - adjusted directory invalidation so file tree refresh could walk upward to the nearest loaded ancestor instead of only refreshing the immediate parent

2. Follow-up fix for Windows e2e failure
   - the PR initially triggered a Windows e2e failure in `e2e/prompt/prompt-mention.spec.ts`
   - I reproduced that locally and traced it to two things:
     - file search could return an empty result before the initial file index finished
     - Windows file search / fuzzy matching was still inconsistent between `\` and `/`
   - I added a fix so the first search waits for initial indexing and the search side compares normalized separators consistently
   - after that, the Windows `@mention` failure passed in CI

3. Follow-up fix for Linux e2e failure
   - after the Windows failure was fixed, CI still failed on Linux in `e2e/session/session-composer-dock.spec.ts`, specifically `blocked question flow unblocks after submit`
   - that one was not failing in app logic; it was timing out while seeding a pending question request for the test
   - I traced that to the test using a live model-driven seed path for question requests, while the sibling permission tests already used deterministic route mocks
   - I rewrote the question-dock tests to use mocked `/question` list/reply/reject endpoints so the test only exercised the dock behavior instead of depending on an LLM/tool round-trip
   - that spec passed locally after the change

Why I closed the PR anyway

- even after the Windows mention fix and the Linux question-dock stabilization attempt, I still could not get the overall PR into a state where I was confident enough to keep asking CI to validate guesses
- my local Windows environment also had unrelated noise that made iteration expensive:
  - the known symlink problem around `packages/app/src/custom-elements.d.ts` and `packages/enterprise/src/custom-elements.d.ts`
  - local full e2e instability unrelated to the original watcher bug
- at that point I had already spent far too much token / debugging budget on the submission and stopped rather than continuing to churn CI with low confidence

What I was able to confirm with high confidence

- the original watcher/open-tab problem is real
- `normalize()` preserving native separators on Windows is definitely part of the problem
- watcher refresh behavior also has a separate gap for directory invalidation / refresh
- fixing the watcher bug exposed or intersected with at least one additional Windows path/search issue in `prompt-mention.spec.ts`
- there was also a flaky Linux e2e in the same PR attempt, but that one looked like test seeding instability rather than the watcher bug itself

What I was not able to deliver confidently

- a final upstream PR that fixed the watcher issue and also left the full CI suite in a clearly green, low-risk state
- a clean separation between "watcher fix side effects" and "pre-existing flaky CI" that I would be comfortable asking maintainers to trust without further iteration

If someone takes another run at this, my recommendation would be:

1. keep the watcher/path fix itself as small as possible

```

keybind = enter=text:\n
keybind = ctrl+enter=text:\r
```
For keybind-related issues, please also check our pinned keybinds documentation: #4997

I've been driving claude code more lately and it's adequate but it does this inexplicable terminal scrollback clearing operation when auto-compacting. Once it compacts you can't even scroll up anymore to see what you were in the middle of doing... Claude Code in general is just a bad example for approach. Yeah it does better than codex, which infuriatingly garbles the terminal and the recent response if you look at it the wrong way, but for CC as far as the approach goes I think it's vastly inferior to opencode's opentui. CC leverages the terminal's scrollback, yeah, but it means horizontally resizing the terminal of a long session causes CC to re-layout and re-emit the entire session out again. It does guarantee the scrollback remains pristine, but it's a heck of a lot of wasted CPU cycles when in truth only the page of what you're viewing right now needs that re-layout to be performed. OpenTUI excels at this in a way only few other apps do (e.g. neovim)

When the autocompact forcibly clears terminal scrollback, that also means you cannot do a (terminal native) search back in there...
